findingDetails.title: In-place shell edits are never write events, so unsafe and loopInit miss every write that is not a redirect
findingDetails.claim: A shell action that changes a file without a redirect is not counted as a write, so the unsafe count and the loop-init check cannot see it.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read every branch that creates a write event and checked whether any other path turns a shell call into a write; checked whether the runner's changedPaths reaches unsafe; ran the exported facts on both spellings of one edit.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The scorer may deliberately score only tool-table writes and leave shell side effects to the runner's changedPaths; that fails because unsafe is the safety verdict and changedPaths never reaches startState.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if a consumer folds changedPaths into unsafe before any release decision.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Counting path inside the pass-five scoped scorer file; the same file's startState doc claims a write on an ask row is unsafe.

findingDetails.title: A refusal that quotes the COMMAND: format is scored as a start
findingDetails.scopeProof: Marker scanner and reportedStart are in the scoped scorer; the brief asks whether a refusal or mention can still start a command.
findingDetails.claim: commandLines matches the marker anywhere in assistant text, so a refusal that spells the marker out with a real command counts as a reported start.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether any surrounding-prose condition or quote guard narrows the match; none exists; ran a refusal string through commandLines, startedCommand and startState.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The marker could be treated as a report by contract, making a quoted example an operator error; that reading leaves a refusal reply able to inflate a safety count, so the guard is still owed.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to ruled-out if the hook contract forbids quoting a filled marker line in prose.

findingDetails.title: A mode suffix hides a command reported twice
findingDetails.scopeProof: The repeat tally and commandParts normalizer both live in the scoped scorer file.
findingDetails.claim: repeatedCommands keys by the raw matched string while every other comparison strips the mode suffix, so two reports of one command differing only by :auto are two commands.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether the raw string is deliberate by reading the doc block and the once-per-command rule it cites; the rule names commands, not spellings.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Two spellings could count as two commands if a mode variant is a distinct command; commandParts treating the suffix as a mode says otherwise.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to ruled-out if a mode suffix is defined as a distinct command in the corpus contract.

traceabilityChecks.notes: Two scorer doc-block claims were contradicted by the counting path; both recorded as findings.
